title: Similarly built animals jump to the same height regardless of size
look_for_in_this_kingdom: jump height and take-off velocity compilations (insects, frogs, mammals, fleas, locusts, humans), Scholz and Alexander style cross-species data
variables_needed: take-off velocity or jump height per individual

claims.label: Similarly built animals should jump to the same absolute height regardless of size
claims.statement: Because the impulse of a leap is proportional to muscle volume and so to body mass, the take-off velocity is independent of size, and similarly built animals should jump to the same actual height rather than the same relative height; longer levers in larger animals give them some advantage.
claims.quote: in other words, that all animals, provided always that they are similarly fashioned, with their various levers etc., in like proportion, ought to jump, not to the same relative, but to the same actual height.

datasets.name: What explains vast differences in jumping power within a clade? Diversity, ecology, and evolution of anuran jumping power (Intraspecific_dataset.xlsx)

other_kingdoms_hint.fossils: fossil jumpers or reconstructions (salientians, fossil insects, leaping mammals) with limb and body dimensions; say plainly when thin
